Example agent handles only cancel_order despite the stated three tools; the printed code is incomplete (variable names first/second missing, assert syntax truncated) and uses model name 'gpt-5' with a ChatOpenAI call style that is not valid LangChain.
Evaluation is shown as a two-assert smoke test; real metrics deferred to Chapter 9.
MCP is described as injecting context without tool invocation, which differs from common usage as a tool/resource protocol.
Text says 'three common design patterns' but lists two (single and multiagent).
practices: Scope to a clear bounded workflow with concrete inputs and structured outputs (Our First Agent System).
An untested agent is an untrusted agent; measure tool precision, parameter accuracy and task success over hundreds of examples (Our First Agent System).
Use large models for open-ended tasks and small models for well-defined repetitive tasks (Model Selection).
Use hybrid strategies or dynamic model routing to balance cost and quality (Model Selection).
Compare candidate models on your own task for best price per performance; benchmarks are only guidance (Model Selection).
Revisit model selection over time (Model Selection).
Build each tool as a self-contained replaceable module (Tool Integration and Modularity).
Short-term memory via rolling context windows; long-term via databases, knowledge graphs or fine-tuned models; prioritise recent data and allow forgetting (Memory).
Orchestrators build plans incrementally and reassess after a few steps (Orchestration).
Scale GPU use with dynamic allocation, elastic provisioning, priority queuing, async execution, load balancing, burst scaling (Scalability).
Reliability needs fault tolerance, extensive testing, monitoring and feedback loops (Reliability).
Prefer lean models, cloud resources and open source where adequate (Costs).
Start with a single agent for narrow tasks; multiagent adds specialisation and parallelism but higher token use and coordination cost (Architecture Design Patterns).
Iterate: prototype quickly, test and gather feedback, refine (Iterative Design).
Evaluate correctness, boundary cases, task metrics, generalisation, user feedback (NPS, CSAT, completion, explicit and implicit signals), human-in-the-loop and end-to-end (Evaluation Strategy).
Roll out in phases, monitor KPIs, collect feedback, iterate (Real-World Testing).
